items.originalTitle: Kolibri is an open-weight LLM from Aleph Alpha for German and English
items.summary:
Aleph Alpha has launched Kolibri, a large language model with 78 billion parameters that uses a mixture-of-experts architecture to activate only about 3.5 billion parameters per token. Trained from scratch on infrastructure in Germany and Finland, Kolibri supports German and English and is released under the Apache 2.0 license with weights available on Hugging Face. The model was designed with the EU AI Act in mind to balance innovation and regulation, allowing organizations to deploy it on-premises with full data privacy and intellectual property control.

Kolibri features 50 layers each containing 384 experts, with a router selecting six experts per token to reduce computation while maintaining model capacity. Its tokenizer is optimized for German compound words, using a large vocabulary of 128,000 tokens trained with a new UniBPE algorithm. Aleph Alpha emphasizes Kolibri's sovereignty, meaning it was developed under European law without foreign control, and it complies with the EU's General-Purpose AI Code of Practice. The model aims to provide a more efficient and privacy-conscious alternative for German and English language tasks.

items.title: Researchers develop Ataraxos AI that beats top Stratego player using a neural network to infer hidden pieces and strategic self-play [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
items.summary:
A team from Carnegie Mellon, MIT, NYU, and Stanford created Ataraxos, an AI that defeated Pim Niemeijer, a leading Stratego player, by 15 wins to one with four draws. The AI uses a second neural network to predict opponents' hidden pieces and employs strategic self-play over 163 million games to master the imperfect-information game.

Stratego's complexity arises from hidden piece identities and long game length, making it challenging for previous AIs like DeepMind's DeepNash. Ataraxos overcomes this by sampling plausible opponent piece arrangements and planning moves accordingly, enabling it to bluff and recover from losing positions methodically. The AI's calm, unbothered approach contrasts with human impulsiveness, contributing to its success against top human competition.

Robinson also emphasized the need for broader cultural changes and stronger external incentives to ensure AI alignment with human values as systems become more capable.

items.title: Report: AI chips shipped through 2027 could run up to 170 million concurrent frontier-model agents, supplying work hours equivalent to hundreds of millions of full-time employees [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How many AI agents could run on the AI chips shipped through 2027?
items.summary:
AI chips shipped through 2027 have the potential to run tens to hundreds of millions of concurrent AI agents, providing work hours comparable to 140 to 720 million full-time employees, according to an analysis by Epoch AI. More efficient models could support billions of agents, but realizing this capacity would require a massive increase in global demand for AI services, with estimated annual API-equivalent spending reaching trillions of dollars.

The analysis estimates that high-bandwidth memory (HBM) shipped from 2025 to 2027 could support 30 to 170 million concurrent agents, assuming full deployment. These agents can operate continuously, working 168 hours per week compared to a human's 40-hour workweek, amplifying their potential economic impact. However, even using 20% of this capacity would imply annual spending of $2.6 to $5.3 trillion, far exceeding current developer revenues projected to reach about $1 trillion by 2027.

The key uncertainty remains whether demand for AI services will grow rapidly enough to utilize this hardware capacity. The report also highlights significant variation in hourly agent costs across different AI models and workloads, underscoring the complexity of scaling AI agent deployment at this scale.

items.originalTitle: AI Agents Need a System of Record, Not Just a Dashboard
items.summary:
Multisynapse argues that managing AI agents requires a system of record that tracks every agent's version, permissions, and actions to ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance. Unlike dashboards that only show what happened, this system provides governance by recording what was allowed and what actually occurred, enabling quick answers to questions about agent behavior and decisions.

The system includes features such as version control, policy checks, graded evaluations before deployment, and tamper-evident audit trails. It supports multi-tenant organizations with role separation and access controls, and maps evidence to standards like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001. This approach aims to provide reliable records for audits and regulatory inquiries, improving trust and control over AI agent operations.

items.originalTitle: Google Updates Guidelines to Punish Sites That Use Fake Bylines and AI-Generated Headshots
items.summary:
Google has revised its content guidelines to explicitly prohibit the use of fabricated creator profiles, including AI-generated headshots, fake names, and false credentials, stating that such deceptive practices make pages untrustworthy and lower their ranking in search results. This update follows investigations into companies like Brown Brothers Media, which used fake journalists and plagiarized content to generate high traffic through AI-powered content mills.

The new guidelines emphasize that accurate authorship information aligns with Google's standards for experience, expertise, authoritativeness, and trustworthiness (E-E-A-T), while deceptive authorship signals low-quality content to both users and Google's automated systems. This move aims to curb the spread of misleading content, although concerns remain about the broader impact of AI-generated summaries on independent journalism and original reporting.
